subject: using multiple palettes or color override

messages.author: daf017f67eba24e8
messages.subject: using multiple palettes or color override
parts:
I've attached the plot i want to tweak, but I'm totally clueless about how to proceed. A shove in the right direction would be appreciated.

You'll see two rows of boxplots in each facet. I want to make the lower one in just gray but leave the boxes there. I also dont want to add the color to the legend.

I could just leave the data, but it seems too busy. I want to highlight the new/better data with color while rendering the old data gray. I know you'll probably try to dissuade me from doing this.... but I'm still curious.

I've tried some random things, scoured the book and tried searching the archives. Nothing has seemed relevant.

The call which creates this plot is

plot.full.R2.RB <-
  ggplot(Atempstats ,aes(nobs,R2,colour=model)) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept=0),size=hline.size)+
  geom_boxplot(data=tempstats,aes(nobs,R2,colour=model),
               outlier.colour=outlier.colour, outlier.size=outlier.size) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.colour=outlier.colour, outlier.size=outlier.size) +
  facet_wrap(~level)+
  opts(title='RS predicts RB')  +
  theme_bw() +
  ylim(-.15,.8) +
  opts(panel.grid.major=theme_line(linetype=grid.line.type,
                                   colour='grey50',size=grid.line.size))


TIA,
JM

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: using multiple palettes or color override
parts:
Hi James,

That sounds like a reasonable idea to me, and to achieve it, all you
need to do is set the colour in the first layer to grey:

geom_boxplot(data=tempstats,outlier.colour=outlier.colour,
outlier.size=outlier.size, colour = "grey50")

Hadley
